name: Dogeforces
description: The Dogeforces company has $$$k$$$ employees. Each employee, except for lower-level employees, has at least $$$2$$$ subordinates. Lower-level employees have no subordinates. Each employee, except for the head of the company, has exactly one direct supervisor. The head of the company is a direct or indirect supervisor of all employees. It is known that in Dogeforces, each supervisor receives a salary strictly more than all his subordinates. The full structure of the company is a secret, but you know the number of lower-level employees and for each pair of lower-level employees, the salary of their common supervisor is known (if there are several such supervisors, then the supervisor with the minimum salary). You have to restore the structure of the company.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 500$$$) — the number of lower-level employees. This is followed by $$$n$$$ lines, where $$$i$$$-th line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_{i,1}, a_{i,2}, \dots, a_{i,n}$$$ ($$$1 \le a_{i,j} \le 5000$$$) — salary of the common supervisor of employees with numbers $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$. It is guaranteed that $$$a_{i,j} = a_{j,i}$$$. Note that $$$a_{i,i}$$$ is equal to the salary of the $$$i$$$-th employee.
output_specification: In the first line, print a single integer $$$k$$$ — the number of employees in the company. In the second line, print $$$k$$$ integers $$$c_1, c_2, \dots, c_k$$$, where $$$c_i$$$ is the salary of the employee with the number $$$i$$$. In the third line, print a single integer $$$r$$$ — the number of the employee who is the head of the company. In the following $$$k-1$$$ lines, print two integers $$$v$$$ and $$$u$$$ ($$$1 \le v, u \le k$$$) — the number of the employee and his direct supervisor. Note that the lower-level employees have numbers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, and for the rest of the employees, you have to assign numbers from $$$n+1$$$ to $$$k$$$. If there are several correct company structures, you can print any of them.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1494D — Dogeforces [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
